chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Samaan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer on Friday, so he said: 'As for [praying] with the Imam, it is two rak'ahs. And as for whoever prays alone, it is four rak'ahs, in the manner of Dhuhr. He means: if there is an Imam who is delivering the sermon, but if there is no Imam delivering the sermon, it is four rak'ahs, even if they pray as a congregation.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the manner of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: What is the number of rak'ahs for Friday prayer when there is no Imam delivering the sermon?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the structural flexibility of Friday prayer, distinguishing between the congregational obligation led by an Imam (two rak'ahs) and the individual or non-imam-led performance (four rak'ahs). It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the essence of Jumu'ah can be maintained as a four-rak'ah prayer when the formal khutbah authority is absent, reflecting the practical adaptability of ritual worship in the absence of the Imam.
